findings.text: The doc-procedure exemption is SOUND, not a loophole. The check (selftest.py:4753-4756) exempts a docs home from the shipped-code requirement ONLY when status == procedure; a mechanical/reference entry with a docs home is rejected (I proved this: flipping branch_protection_recipe from procedure to mechanical while keeping the docs/plugin.md home turns selftest RED). The docs home must still exist in the repo (the exists check runs for all entries). Only two entries use it - branch_protection_recipe (docs/plugin.md) and rollback_drills (docs) - both genuinely documented procedures, not mechanical capabilities. Residual (low): the exemption trusts the status label, so a future mechanical capability deliberately mislabeled status: procedure with a docs home could dodge the shipped check. Mitigated because the known dogfood/build statuses are separately pinned by selftest assertions (~selftest.py:4680-4695) and mislabeling is a deliberate lie a reviewer catches; worth a guard only if the manifest grows a real procedure-with-non-doc-home pattern.

By design (the AC5/AC6 byte-identical requirement) the adopter-facing plugin/templates/.warp/capabilities.yaml still ENUMERATES the 17 repo-only entries, each carrying the explicit 'scope: repo-only' marker. This is honest (the entries are marked as not-shipped-to-adopters, not over-claimed) and is exactly what the spec mandates, so it is not a defect - noted only so a reader knows the adopter manifest lists repo-only items rather than omitting them.

summary: WARP-0906 (docs made true + honest capabilities manifest, W6 of PLAN-0009) passes with notes at 97c4ac2. All 6 ACs confirmed by adversarial probes in an isolated umask-002 worktree. The gate is GREEN (selftest 1350/0, GATE line on the reviewed commit), docs sweeps pass, all 8 capabilities.yaml copies share one sha256, and pack drift is empty for all 7 packs with cross-pack conformance passing. AC5 is the core and its TEETH bite hard end to end: un-marking a dogfood entry (budget_governance) drops selftest to 1338/12, pointing a shipped entry's home at a missing file drops it to 1339/11, and - the strongest probe - pointing a shipped unmarked entry (metrics_dashboard) at a file that EXISTS in the repo but does NOT ship (.warp/budget.py) also goes RED, proving the check enforces SHIP-truth rather than mere file existence. Ship-truth is computed from pack.py engine_files (dynamically imported), not a hardcoded glob, so it stays honest as the engine changes. I independently recomputed the repo-only set and it matches the builder's 17 EXACTLY: every marked entry genuinely does not ship, zero unmarked non-doc entries fail to ship, tracker_routing (.warp/tracker.py) and tracker_routing_enforcement (.warp/validate.py) are correctly left unmarked because they ship, and zero genuinely-shipped capabilities are wrongly marked repo-only. The doc-procedure exemption is sound - only status==procedure may use a docs home and a mechanical/reference entry with a docs home is rejected (proven RED). AC1-AC4 docs claim only what W1-W5 shipped: README version is 3.4.0 with no 3.5.0/Fleet-v1 release claim, no external supervisor (W7) is claimed, every warp CLI flag the docs cite (including --account) exists in bin/warp, and no operating metric appears on the adopter surface. AC6 is clean: no protected path edited, no evidence files in the impl commit, index regenerated, warp name unchanged. RULE #1 is clean - no em/en dashes and no bare double-hyphen in the new prose or markers (all '--' are real --account flags, --- fences, a # --- comment, or a backtick reference). Two non-blocking notes: the docs exemption trusts the status label (low residual, mitigated by pinned statuses), and the byte-identical adopter manifest honestly enumerates the repo-only entries by design. Verdict: pass_with_notes.
